section: Iterate - change: commit-time 80% hook measures requirement coverage
title: Commit hook gates on requirement coverage from the committed manifest
context: check_rtm_coverage read the RTM line for build sections with a commit; adopted projects have none, so the hook allowed every commit silently. Unit U9 of the finalization-claims-hardening campaign.
decision: The hook reads .shipwright/compliance/test-traceability.json (never regenerated): FR coverage gates, AC coverage is reported, unmeasurable cases emit a visible WARN, optional rtm_coverage_baseline ratchets the threshold.
consequences: Measured: FR 21/21 (100%), AC 246/285 (86%, AC inventory from the spec), so no ratchet needed. A manifest older than 14 days or 300 commits WARNs; the legacy section line applies only when no manifest file exists. Accepted risk: the by-commit join of bindings to results is the collector's, not re-verified here; the staleness WARN mitigates.
rationale: A gate named for requirement coverage must measure it; the manifest already joins bindings to execution results. Option A needs no new mechanism, only a pure module in the hook's plugin.
rejected: B: emit a requirement line from rtm_generator (764 LOC, at bloat cap). C: correct the docs only, leaving a gate that never fires. Reading git HEAD instead of the working-tree file: rejected, adds a subprocess.
